title: The 50 Best Mariachi Songs of All Time, Ranked: Staff Picks
summary: From “Mujeres Divinas” to “Guadalajara” and “La Bikina,” these anthems of love, heartbreak and celebration keep Mexico’s Jalisco-rooted tradition alive.
contentText:
Mariachi can break your heart, can make you reach for another drink — and then have an entire room singing at the top of its lungs moments later. Few musical traditions hold that contradiction as powerfully: The grief is theatrical, the romance is all-consuming and the celebration is impossible to resist.

To celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month, kicking off Tuesday (Sept. 15) — as well as Mexico’s Independence Day on Sept. 16 —  Billboard Latin and Billboard Español present the 50 Best Mariachi Songs of All Time.

Born in western Mexico and rooted in Guadalajara, Jalisco, mariachi rose from regional folk tradition to national symbol. It reached an even wider audience during the Golden Age of Mexican Cinema, which begins with the 1936 film Allá En El Rancho Grande , which featured the title song performed by singer and actor Tito Guízar — who graced the cover of Billboard in 1946. Mariachi music flourished during this era, but began to evolve in style and reach by the mid-1950s.

The music’s mythology was also shaped by stars like Jorge Negrete , Pedro Infante and Antonio Aguilar , whose voices, films and charro personas helped transform mariachi into a defining expression of Mexican identity. Later, ensembles such as Mariachi Vargas de Tecalitlán brought greater structure, precision and grandeur to the sound, arranging its violins, trumpets, guitars, vihuela, harp and guitarrón with the scale and drama of an elite symphonic orchestra.

But mariachi has never belonged only to the past. Vicente Fernández carried its emotional force to audiences around the world, while Luis Miguel , Rocío Dúrcal , Juan Gabriel , Chavela Vargas and countless other artists expanded its expressive range. Today, a new generation — including Ángela Aguilar , Alex Fernández , Camila Fernández , Lupita Infante and Majo Aguilar — is introducing mariachi-rooted music to younger listeners, bringing fresh perspectives to a tradition built on lineage, interpretation and reinvention.

That evolution also explains why Christian Nodal earns a place here. Nodal has described his music as mariacheño, a fusion of mariachi and norteño that incorporates accordion while remaining deeply respectful of mariachi’s foundations. As he once said , he studied the tradition and wanted to develop his own sound, without disrespecting the artists who recorded mariachi “as it should be recorded and interpreted.”

Ranked from essential standards to modern reiterations, these are songs that have serenaded lovers, accompanied celebrations, carried people through grief and kept Mexico’s musical heart beating across generations.

Here are our 50 Best Mariachi Songs of All Time, ranked from No. 50 to our No. 1 favorite. — Isabela Raygoza
